english: The parabola $y=x^{2}$ and the line $y=2x+3$ meet at the points $A$ and $B$. Let $C$ be the point on the arc $AB$ of the parabola at which the area of the triangle $ABC$ is the greatest. Then the area of the part of the region bounded by the parabola and the line $AB$ which lies outside the triangle $ABC$ is equal to
hindi: परवलय $y=x^{2}$ तथा रेखा $y=2x+3$ बिन्दुओं $A$ तथा $B$ पर मिलते हैं। माना कि $C$ परवलय के चाप $AB$ पर वह बिन्दु है जिस पर त्रिभुज $ABC$ का क्षेत्रफल अधिकतम है। तब परवलय तथा रेखा $AB$ द्वारा परिबद्ध क्षेत्र के उस भाग का क्षेत्रफल, जो त्रिभुज $ABC$ के बाहर है, बराबर है
solution: Area of $ABC$ is greatest when $C$ is farthest from $AB$, i.e. where the tangent is parallel to $AB$: $2x=2\Rightarrow C(1,1)$.

Segment area $=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{3}(2x+3-x^{2})\,dx=\dfrac{32}{3}$; by Archimedes' result it equals $\dfrac43$ of triangle $ABC$, so the triangle has area $8$ (direct check: $\frac12|(-1)(1-9)+1(9-1)+3(1-1)|=8$).
solution_full: For $C(c,c^{2})$ with $-1<c<3$, the area of $ABC$ is $\frac12|AB|$ times the distance of $C$ from $AB$; the distance is proportional to $2c+3-c^{2}$, which is greatest at $c=1$, where the tangent slope $2c$ equals the slope $2$ of $AB$. So $C=(1,1)$.
Region between the parabola and $AB$: Area $=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{3}(2x+3-x^{2})\,dx=\left[x^{2}+3x-\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{-1}^{3}=9-\left(-\dfrac{5}{3}\right)=\dfrac{32}{3}$.

Triangle $ABC$: $\dfrac12\left|(-1)(1-9)+1(9-1)+3(1-1)\right|=\dfrac12\cdot 16=8$. This agrees with Archimedes' result that the segment is $\frac43$ of this triangle (equivalently $\frac23$ of the circumscribing parallelogram): $\frac43\cdot 8=\frac{32}{3}$.
The triangle lies inside the segment (its vertices are on the boundary of the convex segment), so the part outside the triangle has area $\dfrac{32}{3}-8=\dfrac{8}{3}$.
Check: this part is the two smaller segments on the chords $AC$ ($y=1$) and $CB$ ($y=4x-3$), each of area $\dfrac{2^{3}}{6}=\dfrac43$.
originality_note: New: the first step of Archimedes' exhaustion asked as an area question - the leftover between a parabolic segment and its greatest inscribed triangle (way 1, one step of the iteration). Closest known: area of the segment cut from y = x^2 by a line. Different because: C must be identified by the maximal-triangle condition and the 4/3 ratio (or the two small segments) gives the answer.

concept_use.Area of a parabolic segment (Archimedes': The segment is 4/3 of triangle ABC (2/3 of the parallelogram), giving 32/3 - 8; equivalently two small segments of 4/3 each.
concept_use.Area bounded by two curves: The region between y = x^2 and y = 2x + 3 from x = -1 to 3 has area 32/3.

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve and symbol introduced, region named by its bounding curves, one reading, answer unique and equal to the plan; options of one form; Hindi mirrors the English maths. Checked that the maximal triangle has C at x = 1 and that the triangle lies inside the segment. Distractors are one small segment, the whole segment and a slip. No change.
key_step: C is the point where the tangent is parallel to AB; segment minus triangle.
justification: Three routine steps (intersections, maximal-triangle point, segment minus triangle) with a well-known ratio; like 2024-P2-Q2 (L2).
blueprint_concepts: Area of a parabolic segment (Archimedes' 2/3 result)
